author: blu
body: Do NOT restore a binary search here. This was one until 2026-07-28 (main 11369) and it silently found only some of its names: a binary search requires the list to be ordered by the comparison it searches with, and the list is written alphabetically while text-compare orders by CCE, which numbers letters by frequency. `c` is 24 and `f` is 43, so `char-at` sorts before `file-exists` under the comparator and after it in the list. Names past the first inversion were unreachable, and an unreachable builtin does not fail loudly -- it falls through to the ordinary apply path and emits a call to a function the target language has never heard of. Measured per plug by codex/plugs/test-input/builtin-reach.codex, a probe that cites nothing so its calls reach this table. Thirteen plugs carried the defect. A linear scan has no ordering invariant to get wrong and this runs once per call site at transpile time.
